A space charge limited current density of 33.3 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 1000degC has been obtained by using 587 nm Sc<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-doped W powders.

articleTitle: Growth rate of the Coaxial Slow Wave Structure
abstract: The growth rate of the Coaxial Slow Wave Structure is studied through a simple method employing the relativistic Newton's equation, the driving Maxwell equations and the linear assumption of the small signals. In addition, effects of the electron kinetic energy and the beam current on the growth rate are investigated preliminarily.

articleTitle: Experimental progress on the development of a multiple-beam klystron with 13% bandwidth
abstract: We present recent progress on the development of a multiple-beam klystron (MBK) designed to operate in S-band with a 1-dB bandwidth of 13%. The amplifier is powered by an 18-beam electron gun operating at a voltage of 42 kV and a total current of 41.6 A. Measured gun voltage-current characteristics will be compared with the design predictions made by the 3D particle code, MICHELLE. Experimental measurements of the frequency and Q's of individual cavities comprising the interaction circuit will be compared with 3D electromagnetic simulations. Finally, as available, we will also report on hot test measurements of the rf performance of the MBK.

articleTitle: Design of vane loaded helical slow-wave structures for broad-band traveling-wave tubes
abstract: In this work, we attempted to obtain a collection of useful results to guide the design of broadband helical slow-wave structures. A 3D eigensolver was used to model vane loaded slow-wave structures. Plots of phase velocity and interaction impedance as function of a normalized frequency were taken varying some geometric parameters. The result is a collection of plots showing how the vane geometry affects the dispersion and the interaction impedance profiles of a helical slow-wave structure.

articleTitle: Improved flexibility by in-orbit-adjustable saturation output power of TWTs
abstract: A substantial number of applications require operation of Travelling Wave Tube Amplifiers (TWTAs) and Microwave Power Modules (MPMs) at saturation to take benefit from the stable RF power and insensitivity to input power variations. Due to the usual end-of-life margins and performance spread over frequency and units the saturation point is typically much higher than really needed for a particular channel. This paper shows how the RF power and therewith the DC power can be optimized for individual MPMs in orbit by telecommand with no change of the saturation characteristics while maintaining RF input power and linearity characteristics. It also shows the typical linearity performance over the adjustment range.

articleTitle: Extended interaction multiple beam klystrons simulation with DEV 5.0 code
abstract: In this report the extensions of DEV 5.0 code including extended interaction multiple beam klystrons (EIMBK) simulation with identical and non-identical beams are presented. The features of the computational model are discussed.

articleTitle: Development of a C-band broadband klystron
abstract: This paper reports the design, simulation and test results of a C-band broadband klystron, which was developed by the Institute of Electronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IECAS) from March 2005 to June 2008. The typical result is over 800 kW peak output power and 30% conversion efficiency of beam-to-RF among a 400 MHz bandwidth under 5.25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>/<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</sub> RF duty cycle. The overall length of the tube is 702 mm, and its weight is about 22 kg.

articleTitle: 2 to 18 GHz, MPM-based high-power transmitter suite for military airborne ECM applications
abstract: This paper describes the development effort for a very compact suite of high-power transmitters for military airborne electronic countermeasure (ECM) applications. The suite consists of four individual MPM-based, 2 to 7 GHz and 6 to 18 GHz, CW and pulse transmitters covering the 2 to 18 GHz frequency range. Each transmitter is a compact line replaceable unit (LRU) with all associated features. dB Control developed, tested, and qualified this transmitter suite in 15 months. This paper's primary emphasis is on the design of highly reliable, vacuum electron device (VED) products for extreme environments, and also includes details of development and qualification activities. In conclusion, the paper outlines current production activities of this transmitter suite.

articleTitle: An in situ emission microscopy study of barium supply to the surface of scandium-coated porous tungsten
abstract: The transport of Ba to the surface of a porous tungsten disk packed with barium oxide powder is observed directly with emission microscopy. The W disk surface is patterned with sputter deposited scandium metal squares. Thermionic electron emission is observed from the Ba/Sc/W areas at temperatures below those required for thermionic electron emission from the non-Sc coated areas. The ldquodispensingrdquo process is observed directly, in situ.

articleTitle: Particle-in-cell simulation of helix traveling-wave tube
abstract: A 2.5-D electromagnetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation code has been used to study the nonlinear beam-wave interaction of a helix traveling-wave tube (TWT). The simulation model is developed with the PIC code MAGIC. The nonlinear process is simulated and analyzed. The simulation results meet the measurements very well, including the output power and gain.

articleTitle: Design study of magnetron injection guns for a 4 MW 170 GHz coaxial gyrotron
abstract: At the Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe (FZK), the feasibility of a 4 MW 170 GHz gyrotron is currently under investigation. The project aims inter alia at increasing the output power of coaxial gyrotrons to their technical and physical limits. For this purpose, a design of a triode type electron gun is presented which has been optimized to meet the required specifications for the operating mode of a 4 MW continuous-wave gyrotron. Simulations indicate suitable performance with respect to beam quality and reliability.

articleTitle: A 20 kW X band High Power Amplifier for ESA Deep Space Ground Stations
abstract: The European Space Agency (ESA) is developing a network of 35 m antennas for Telemetry, Tracking and Command (TT&C) operations of primarily Deep Space spacecraft. A 20 kW water cooled X-band Klystron-based High Power Amplifier (HPA) working in the bandwidth 7145-7235 MHz , complete with power supply, internal protection, cooling system, local and remote monitor and control has been designed and developed by Rheinmetall Italia SpA, Roma (hereafter referred as RhI) in the contest of the ESOC contract 18570/04/D/SW . The complete HPA or parts of it will be installed in the Antenna Equipment Room (AER) of ESA Deep Space Ground Stations (DSGS). This paper describes the needs satisfied by the unit, the main technical performances and the main test results.

articleTitle: Development of tri-band helix TWT for telecommunications using “Semi-metallic Rods” structure
abstract: Telecommunication transmission systems require high power linear amplifiers operating in C, X and Ku bands due to the necessity to manage a large amount of information. The helix TWT amplifier is the device adequate for this application since it can provide wide bandwidth and high power level at high frequencies. Selex Galileo is developing a high power helix TWT operating from C to Ku band using the novel RF interaction structure "Semi-metallic Rods ". The test results of the first electrical model are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: 100GHz LIGA-fabricated coupled-cavity device
abstract: This abstract describes the design, fabrication and testing of microfabricated 100 GHz coupled-cavity backward wave oscillator (CCBWO), which is operated in space harmonics -1 at 12 kV and 50 mA with round-beam radius 0.18 mm. The RF performance has studied using 3-D electromagnetic field simulator and particle-in-cell code. The cold-test assembly has been fabricated. The complete device assembly for hot-test is under fabrication. Experimental results will be presented.

articleTitle: 1558151 first gain demonstration in an X-band antenna-amplifier
abstract: It is reported about the initial results of the experiments on gain demonstration in the antenna-amplifier, the hybrid device combining a relativistic Cherenkov amplifier and a surface wave antenna. In this device, an annular electron beam amplifies the fundamental, nonaxisymmetric HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode of the dielectric rod antenna. The beam is generated by a compact linear induction accelerator (LIA) module with a hollow knife-edge cathode, and the hollow cathode holder plays also the role of antenna feed waveguide since, due to the principles of LIA operation, it has a ground potential at the external side.

articleTitle: Design of a large compression ratio electron gun and uniform field focusing system for Ka-band exended interaction klystron
abstract: This paper presents an electron gun which have a voltage of 13 kV, current of 0.7 A and large compression ratio of 80. The maximum emitted current density is only 2.2 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.Uniform field focusing system is also designed to keep the trajectories in a good shape while passing through a 40 mm-long channel.

articleTitle: A study of nonlinear oscillation behavior of a driven gyrotron backward-wave oscillator
abstract: This study employed a nonlinear self-consistent time-independent code to analyze a gyro-BWO with an external injected signal. There are three regimes, including amplifier, injection-locking oscillator and mode competition regimes, in the gyro-BWO at different injected powers. In the mode competition regime, there are three steady modes in the injected power range. Based on theory of nonlinear oscillation, the amplifier and injection-locking oscillator modes are the stable modes in the regime. An oscillator plane of the gyro-BWO is elucidated in the paper.

articleTitle: Carbon nanotube based photocathodes for high frequency amplifiers
abstract: The combination of high frequency, high power, high efficiency capabilities is a feature of vacuum tube technology. For most of applications, large bandwidths are required, and therefore the modulation method should also allow large bandwidth operation. Optically modulated cold cathodes, avoiding the use of resonant cavities, should satisfy this requirement. This is the reason why we have developed carbon nanotube based photocathode.

articleTitle: Design study of a two-cavity monotron
abstract: In its classical embodiment, the monotron has its conversion efficiency limited to 20.0%. But we demonstrate here that on considering a stepped electric-field axial profile the monotron efficiency can attain the theoretical maximum value of 57.0%, almost three times as high as that obtained from the conventional uniform field distribution. This is accomplished by using two cavities electromagnetically coupled by an annular slit crossed by an electron stream. From a one-dimensional analysis, a two-cavity monotron is developed to operate in the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub> mode at 4.0 GHz when self-excited by a 20 keV, 10 A hollow electron beam. The device operation is examined through a 2 1/2-D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation giving a 47.5% conversion efficiency. Departure from the theoretically predicted efficiency is explained by beam-thickness effects.

articleTitle: Novel geometry of carbon nanotube field emitter to achieve high current densities for terahertz sources
abstract: We introduce a novel geometry carbon nanotube field emitter array capable of achieving high current densities. Arrays of patterned vertically aligned CNT bundles, with an open center similar to the structure of a donut, was grown directly on bulk metallic substrates. This new carbon nanotube structure, with larger edge area for enhanced edge effect, reached current densities as high as 60 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at an applied DC field of less than 8 V/mum.

articleTitle: Simulation and evaluation of components for a GyroTWA
abstract: The operating performance of a GyroTWA is dependent upon the performance of its constituent components and their compatibility once assembled into a complete device. This paper discusses the evaluation work performed to assess the performance of major GyroTWA sub-assemblies and also resolve potential incompatibility issues that could only be identified through full structure simulation.

articleTitle: Impedance calculation of helical slow-wave structure using HFCS-I and MAFIA
abstract: Using HFCS-I and MAFIA, the impedance characteristics of a typical helical slow-wave structure (SWS) is studied, in which the Non-Resonant Perturbation (NRP) Method is adopted and the direct calculation from discrete Electromagnetic (EM) fields is performed. The results from HFCS-I and MAFIA are found to be consistent.

articleTitle: A THz gyrotron based on a pulse solenoid
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research Inc. (CCR) is developing a THz gyrotron with repetitive pulse capability. The gyrotron is designed to produce radiation up to 5 kW in 10 microsecond pulses from 650 GHz to 1 THz at the fundamental cyclotron resonance and between 1 THz and 2 THz at the second harmonic. The magnetic field is provided by a pulsed solenoid producing up to 37 Tesla. The solenoid is expected to operate at pulse repetition rate of about 1 Hz. A new magnet design and tests of the magnet and gyrotron will be reported.

articleTitle: Diamond current amplifier for spatially-distributed beam generation
abstract: A diamond current amplifier is being developed to provide high-current-density electron beams needed for sheet beam generation. Thin single-crystal CVD diamond films are being grown and optimized with respect to crystal purity, film thickness, and surface quality. Electron emission measurements taken from fabricated amplifiers will be used to characterize and optimize the emission gain, emitted electron energy spread, and spatial uniformity of the emitted beam.

articleTitle: Design of asymmetrical electron beam devices using computer optimization
abstract: Iterative computational design of asymmetrical electron beam devices, such as sheet beam and multiple beam klystrons, requires 3D analysis involving complex geometries. Manual, iterative design is extremely difficult and impractical for all but the simplest devices. Computer optimization tools and techniques are described that provide automated design of these devices using common personal computers with reasonable execution times.

articleTitle: Measurement of the coupling impedance in slow-wave structures using a longitudinally conducting plate
abstract: A method of measuring the coupling impedance in slow-wave structures (SWS) is presented and analyzed in this paper. This method is based on comparisons of the resonant frequencies of a SWS with and without the longitudinally conducting probe. Using these frequencies, we derive an expression for the wave impedance of a sheet electron beam in a planar SWS with a rectangular cross section.

articleTitle: Conceptual design of a 1MW 175MHz CW magnetron
abstract: Advances in the control of CW magnetrons have raised the possibility of using these devices as the RF power sources for particle accelerators. This paper describes the conceptual design of a 1 MW, 175 MHz, CW magnetron and compares its performance with tetrode amplifiers.

articleTitle: Emission property of impregnated cathode with Y2O3 and Sc2O3 co-doped tungsten substrate
abstract: In this paper emission properties of Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and Sc<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> co-doped tungsten matrix impregnated cathodes are discussed.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of 30GHz 4 Cavities Gyroklystron
abstract: This paper reports the result about the 30GHz 4 Cavities Gyroklystron we have designed recently. After lots of optimizing and simulations about the beam-wave interaction in this Gyroklystron, at the coefficient of magnetic field 0.8745, beam voltage 72KV, beam current 15A, and input power 170W, it was observed that the output power of about 340KW with efficiency 31%, gain 33dB and 3dB bandwidth over 330MHz.

articleTitle: Performance of Tungsten wire reservoir cathodes
abstract: Research is continuing on development of controlled porosity cathodes capable of very long life times. Tungsten wires are sintered to form a material consisting of a uniform pattern of pores to transport barium from a reservoir. The combination of uniform pores and the reservoir results in very uniform current emission from the surface with extremely long life. The barium diffusion rate can be controlled by the designer.

articleTitle: Vacuum Microwave Integrated Circuits for radar RF front-end
abstract: A new innovative application of vacuum microwave electronics is suggested. Vacuum Microwave Integrated Circuits (VMIC) is suggested for design of radar front-end with high resistance against radioactivity and high power electromagnetic signals. We describe general approach to design of the VMIC suggested and give preliminary results of its possible implementation and future applications.

articleTitle: Double-gap vircator operation at sub-microsecond pulse duration
abstract: The double-gap S-band vircator operation has been investigated at sub-microsecond duration of the high-current electron beam generated in a planar diode. This version of vircator (see Fig. 1), although driven by a high-current (ges10 kA) relativistic electron beam, nevertheless allows both relatively efficient microwave generation and also radiation frequency stability, due to the use of a single-mode two-section rectangular RF cavity. The double-gap vircator powered by the accelerator SINUS-7 (1 MV, 20 kA, 50 ns) demonstrated ~1GW peak power of microwave radiation in the S-band at ~25 ns pulse length with ~5% efficiency [1]. Earlier experiments with longer driving beam pulses [2] at the voltages close to those of [1] confirmed the constancy of the radiation frequency, as determined by the cavity, during the pulse. However, the microwave pulse was significantly shortened (< 100 ns) as compared to the accelerating voltage pulse that was explained by electron and ion emission from the plasma formed on the cavity walls leading to absorption of the microwave energy. In this work, we present the results of the experiments performed at moderate accelerating voltages, <550 kV, and longer pulse durations, ~500 ns.

articleTitle: The effect of grooved surface on dielectric window multipactor
abstract: Dielectric window breakdown remains a major limiting in transmission of high power microwave (HPM). The effect of surface roughness on multipactor from a periodic rectangular grooved surface under vacuum is investigated by using electromagnetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. The microwave frequency is 2.86 GHz. Vaughan's secondary emission model [3] is used to calculate the secondary electron yield. Electron cloud space distribution, statistic energy and secondary emission yield et al. are analyzed under periodic grooved surface. It is found that grooved surface with some height and width can significantly reduce the secondary emission yield and suppress multipactor.

articleTitle: New grade of temperature compensated samarium cobalt permanent magnets and design considerations
abstract: Electron Energy has successfully developed a new grade of zero Reversible Temperture Coeffeicient (RTC) magnets with maximum energy product, (BH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>, of 18.0 MGOe and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> > 12 kOe. The new grade of zero RTC 18 augments the existing product line and surpasses the prior highest energy zero RTC grade with a (BH)max of 16 MGOe. The RTC of the newly developed magnets is suitable for TWT applications where little change in magnetic induction, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>, over a wide temperature range of up to -50deg to +150degC is desired. Excellent magnetic properties were obtained with reversible temperature coefficients on the order of -0.001% /degC .

articleTitle: Waveguide system for high-power microwave pulse compression
abstract: X-band passive microwave pulse compression is an interesting area of research in vacuum electronics. Applications include radar technology, plasma diagnostics etc. The scientific study of producing high-power nanosecond microwave pulses, using passive sweep-frequency compression, was undertaken. Two novel helically corrugated waveguides were investigated; 3-fold and 5-fold, respectively. The 3-fold structure couples a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.1</sub> travelling wave with a near cut-off TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.1</sub> wave producing a region far from cut-off with a large change in group velocity as a function of frequency. A 2.08 metre long copper helical waveguide was used to compress a 80 ns, 5.5 kW frequency-swept pulse from a high power TWT (TMD PTC6321), driven by an arbitrary waveform generator and vector signal generator, to a 1.5 ns, 135 kW pulse containing -75% of the energy of the input pulse. To enhance the power capabilities of the microwave pulse compressor a more overmoded larger diameter 5-fold helical waveguide structure which adiabatically couples a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.1</sub> traveling wave and a near cut-off TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.2</sub> wave was studied. Analysis of the dispersion characteristics carried out using CST MWS will be presented.

articleTitle: Space charge oscillations in gyrotron magnetron-injection guns with high pitch-factor
abstract: The data of numerical simulation of gyrotron magnetron-injection guns (MIGs) forming helical electron beams (HEBs) with high pitch-factor are presented. The HEBs parameters for the regimes with big value of the locked into the adiabatic trap space charge are found. It is shown that if the magnetic compression ratio or the anode potential is high enough to cause the intense space charge oscillations in the beam, the values of the pitch-factor and velocity spread are saturated while the oscillations of the space charge and potential in the beam continue to increase.

Author Keywords: low frequency space charge and potential oscillations

articleTitle: High efficiency multiple beam klystron (MBK) stability
abstract: This paper describes an extension of the method of moments to allow full solutions of a reentrant cavity for modes with azimuthal variation by coupling the TE and TM solutions at the interface between the two regions. In addition a treatment of MBK stability using wake field theory is proposed.

articleTitle: The study of dispersion shaping and harmonic suppression in helix TWT
abstract: In the helix traveling-wave tube (TWT), the dispersion shaping and harmonic suppression is studied from theory analysis to simulation investigation in this paper. The negative dispersion is formed to suppress the harmonic content by the loaded slow-wave structure (SWS). After the dispersion shaping, the fundamental output power increases about 40 W and the second harmonic level decreases about 6 dB at the low end of the frequency band.

articleTitle: On the prospects of multibeam IOT for linac with efficiency exceeding 80%
abstract: The results of designing and simulation of multibeam klystrode for powering up of linear accelerators are presented. Due to special design of input cavity and operation in class C the tube has CW output power 100 kW, efficiency 80%, gain 30 dB at frequency 1300 MHz and power supply voltage 24 kV.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of pole-controlled electron gun in PPM
abstract: Pulse electron gun is an important part of pulse TWT. The grid-controlled electron gun is not fit for high power pulse TWT and space TWT for its deficiency in stability and long life. Pole-controlled electron gun is a preferable technique. A pole-controlled, hollow-beam electron gun has been successfully designed and fabricated with rigorous calculations and judicious choice of its physical variables. The influence of the electron gun geometry on the hidden variables, including its perveance, its beam waist, and its laminar flow, was evaluated by means of directly measured results and by some theoretical derivation.

articleTitle: Influence of variations of the electrodynamics performances under the attenuator on parameters of Helix TWT
abstract: The variations of phase velocity and coupling impedance under an attenuator of a traveling-wave tube (TWT) are investigated. It is shown, that they reduce, and the coupling impedance is not recovered by increase of a slow-wave structure (SWS) period, that reduces TWT efficiency.

Author Keywords: a phase velocity of a wave

articleTitle: Development of a 350 MHz, 200 kW CW, multiple beam IOT
abstract: Final design and fabrication are in progress on a 350 MHz, 200 kW CW, multiple beam, inductive output tube (IOT). The device includes seven electron guns in a circular array. A single input cavity drives the fields for all seven electron guns. RF power is generated in a single output cavity. The device is predicted to achieve approximately 70% efficiency with 22 dB gain.

articleTitle: PTG1181 electron gun development
abstract: A gridded electron gun was designed to produce a 150 keV electron beam for a gyro TWA amplifier. The gun operates into the magnetic focusing field of the TWA to produce a well collimated beam. This paper describes the design of the gun and testing using a test device designed to test the beam collimation under operating conditions.

articleTitle: Design and test of a 90 kV, low emittance, gridded gun
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research Inc. (CCR) has developed a 1 A, 90 kV electron gun for use as an injector for accelerators. The gun uses a commercial gridded cathode with an external grid driver to produce 10 mus-long pulse trains of 1 ns pulses. The pulse train has a repetition frequency of 36.67 MHz. Detailed simulations were used to minimize the emittance. Results of the simulations and tests of the gun are reported.

articleTitle: Investigation of conductivity loss in a helix slow-wave structure due to the backward-wave space-harmonic propagation mode
abstract: Closed form expression for the inductance per unit length of the transmission-line equivalent circuit of a helical slow-wave structure was derived incorporating the effects of space-harmonic propagating modes and surface current density on the helix over the actual metallic area of the tape. This expression was used for estimating the conductivity loss in the structure following Wheeler's incremental inductance rule. Some interesting characteristics that were observed on the conductivity loss due to the backward-wave space-harmonic mode are reported.

articleTitle: High-power flexible payload architectures for future European broadcasting satellite services
abstract: Promising high-power flexible payload architectures for future European S, Ku and Ka-Band broadcasting satellite services are introduced.

articleTitle: Mechanism of efficiency enhancement in split-cavity electron-wave oscillators
abstract: The two-fold enhancement in the conversion efficiency of a monotron operating in the pi mode-instead of the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub> mode for which the efficiency is limited to 20 percent-arises from a phase synchronization process due the action of RF electric fields of reversed signs in each partition of the bisected cavity.

articleTitle: Perfectly matched boundary condition for helical slow wave structures
abstract: A perfectly matched boundary condition for helical slow wave structures is implemented into a 3D finite-element electromagnetic simulation tool. Results are presented and compared to the results obtained with a method described in the literature[1].

articleTitle: Novel uniform heating topology for thermionic cathodes
abstract: Various methods of bringing thermionic cathodes to full emission temperature are described and compared for both temperature-limited emission and space charge-limited emission. Thermal Radiation Heating (TRH) and Backside Electron-beam Auxiliary Cathode Heating (BEACH) are described along with a novel Directly-Heated Cathode (DHC) design which significantly reduces variations in cathode surface temperature. A comparison of the calculated and measured temperature profiles for this new cathode heating topology using selected prototypes is presented.

articleTitle: Study of phase rematch on overmoded waveguide mode converter
abstract: Based on the mode coupling theory, the design of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>—TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> overmoded circular waveguide mode converter geometric configuration with the different phase rematch and structure is given to obtain more acceptable geometry parameters. The regulation about the radius of the circular waveguides, curvature and frequency of bent circular waveguides and the bandwidth is obtained. The results contribute to design corresponding circular waveguide mode converter with the tight, the efficient and the wideband.

articleTitle: High power 94 GHz amplifier for EarthCARE mission Doppler radar
abstract: EarthCARE (Earth Clouds, Aerosols and Radiation Explorer) is the 6th Earth Explorer Core Mission of the European Space Agency and a joint undertaking with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). It will study and analyze the interaction and impact of clouds and aerosols on the Earth's radiative budget. Along with other instruments, the satellite payload will include a 94 GHz Cloud Profiling Radar (CPR) with Doppler capability. This paper presents the development of a High Power Amplifier for the EarthCARE CPR and reviews HPA requirements, design and performance.

articleTitle: Modeling of an inductive output tube with the MAGIC simulation code
abstract: We describe the simulation of an inductive output tube (IOT) using the particle-in-cell code MAGIC. Simulations were performed to analyze three basic processes in an IOT: formation of bunched electrons beams from a gridded electron gun, interaction between bunched beams and rf field in a resonator, and spent beam collection with a multi-stage depressed collector. There is excellent agreement between simulation results and experimental data.

articleTitle: Research on thermal-electron-emission area source for low-light image intensifier screen testing instrument
abstract: Thermal-electron emission area source is a key component in image intensifier screen testing instrument. On the basis of the analysis of relationship between thermal emission characteristics, the shape of filament and the density of thermal electron emission, electronic area-emitting source is designed. The distribution of electric field and electronic tracks are theoretically analyzed and calculated to make it has features of dispersing, uniform, converging and submerging. By testing a standard screen, correct the structure of thermal electron area sources to meet the requirements of test indexes and obtain reasonable thermal electron emission area sources. Its successful development provides effective technical support to the luminous screen test for uniformity, brightness, luminescence efficiency and afterglow and to the examination of other components (such as MCP parameters)of low-light image intensifier.

articleTitle: Modes in lossy dielectric-loaded metal cylindrical waveguide for gyrotron-traveling-wave amplifier applications
abstract: Using properly designed lossy dielectric-coated metal cylindrical waveguide as the linear amplification stage of a gyrotron-traveling-wave amplifier has been proved to be an effective method to obtain high stability. However, the lossy property of the dielectric material complicates the understanding of the fast-slow-wave property and mode identification. This paper is devoted to reveal in depth the modes in lossy dielectric-coated metal cylindrical waveguide for gyro-TWT amplifier applications.

articleTitle: Research and development in a high-power 6.7 GHz monotron
abstract: This article overviews recent activities carried out in the construction and tests of a 10 kW, 6.7 GHz monotron. In addition to the monotron components- injection electron gun, cavity resonator, and output waveguide-, a hard-tube pulser with three tretrodes in parallel and able to produce negative voltages up to 30 kV/20 A from a positive DC charging power supply is also discussed.

articleTitle: Improved focus performance of triode structure ZnO-FED with a metal grid
abstract: A double gate structure ZnO Field Emission Display (ZnO-FED) is proposed. In this kind of structure, a planar gate electrode is printed onto the cathode plate, it is used to modulate the conductive current from the ZnO emitters; a mesh grid with MgO layer is placed above the cathode plate and as the other gate electrode. Compare to the normal planar triode structure ZnO-FED, the focus performance of this kind of double gate structure is improved apparently. Simulation results show that the electron trajectories have been focalized, and the experimental results show the improvement of light spots of the ZnO-FED.

articleTitle: Frequency doublers with transverse modulation and bunching of the electron beam under inhomogeneous magnetic field
abstract: Potentially effective devices of frequency doublers with transverse modulation of electron beam are considered.

articleTitle: Ba/BaO evaporation measurement during accelerated life test
abstract: The Ba and BaO evaporation rates of a thermionic cathode have been measured at 145K and 170K above the typical operating temperature being about 1033K. According to the measurement result, the relationship between cathode lifetime and operation temperature has been discussed. A comparison life test also be done between a poisoned but reactivated cathode and a normal one under the same condition. We found almost the same emission current at the beginning but different current decrease speed and Ba evaporation rate at the course of the life test.

articleTitle: Role of amorphous phase in electron emission from ferroelectric copolymer P(VDF-TrFE) films
abstract: The ferroelectric copolymer PVDF-TrFE thin films were deposited by spin coating method. Electron emission properties of PVDF-TrFE thin film annealed at 140°C were tested, and the role of amorphous phase in electron emission process was discussed. The results showed that the electron emission ability of PVDF-TrFE film was dependent on the film crystallinty, and amorphous phase in the film determined main electron emission process.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit analysis of out-loaded cavity
abstract: The solution of a parallel equivalent circuit model is calculated for evaluating an out-loaded cavity's frequencies and quality factors, and the analytic results agree well with the numerical simulations. The characters of out-loaded cavity are also analyzed using this model.

articleTitle: Automatic system of measuring dispersion and interaction impedance of Helix SWS
abstract: In order to obtain the parameters of dispersion and interaction impedance of Helix Slow-Wave Structure (SWS), an automatic system was established. A non-resonant perturbation model was employed in the system. The helix SWS under measurement is 1:1 model of practical helix SWS. The hardware of the system is mainly composed of Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), personal computer (PC), moving platform, controller and optical monitor. The special program was developed to control the measure progress and manage the data. The experimental results were in good agreement with the results calculated using Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: MEMS templating technique for miniaturization of carbon nanotube field emission guns
abstract: We demonstrate a novel MEMS technique for fabrication of a well-aligned individual carbon nanotube field emission gun for high-resolution electron beam applications.

articleTitle: Integrated method for simulation of the statistical performances of TWT
abstract: The simulation method of the statistical performances of a traveling wave tube (TWT), that takes into account simultaneously a spread of a constructive-technology factor along the length of the device and their average values from the device to the device is created.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka-band TE11 mode gyrotron traveling-wave amplifier
abstract: A Ka-band gyrotron traveling wave amplifier operating in the TE11 circular mode has been presented. The effects of the parameters such as input power, driver frequency and velocity ratio on the performance of the gyro-TWT ares discussed. The simulation results show that the gain and the bandwidth of the designed Ka-band gyro-TWT is about 54.0 dB and 2.5 GHz with 3 dB bandwidth respectively. The peak output power and the corresponding electron efficiency is about 94 kW and 22.4% respectively with the voltage 70 kV and the current 6 A at the velocity ratio 1.0.

articleTitle: MAGIC electromagnetic FDTD-PIC code dense plasma model comparison with Lsp
abstract: The MAGIC EM FDTD PIC code has been applied to dense plasma air ionization test problems with nominally one percent agreement of the maximum responses versus Lsp.

articleTitle: Study of complex mode converter for 3mm-wave complex cavity Gyrotron
abstract: A complex mode converter consisting of waveguide and quasi-optical mode converters is proposed to utilize high mode-transforming efficiency of the former and compact size of the latter. Radiation patterns of quasi-optical mode converter with TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub> modes as its feeds are got by numerical calculation method based on the theory of vector diffraction integral. These patterns show that the radiation pattern is more similar to the wanted Gauss pattern when the feed takes the mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>. So the conclusion is that the complex mode converter, transforming TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub> mode to TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode by waveguide converter and then TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode to good Gauss pattern, is helpful to hold higher converting efficiency and smaller size than waveguide or quasi-optical one alone.

articleTitle: Microwave sintering and field emission property of CNTs/diamond composite
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/diamond composite were synthesized by microwave-sintering method and the field emission property was studied. The binding energy of two materials become larger and the carbonization of the diamond less, compare to sintering in the common tube furnace. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to evaluate the morphological and the structural features. The CNTs were well-proportioned dispersed in composite and formed emission tip. The results of field emission showed that the field emission of CNTs/diamond composite was improved, the current density reached 15 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, compare to sintering in a horizontal tube furnace (0.88 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: 8mm high power TE01—TM11 mode converter in overmoded waveguide
abstract: Based on the mode coupling theory, design of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>—TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode converter geometry configuration with traditional waveguide axis constant curvature and improved waveguide axis sinusoidal curvature is given for more acceptable geometry parameters. The conversion efficiency of 8mm high-power circular waveguide with waveguide axis sinusoidal curvature is about 99% with bandwidth of 32%.

articleTitle: Field emission from vertically aligned indium tin oxide tip array
abstract: A novel fabrication method of high aspect ratio indium tin oxide (ITO) nano tip array which has the advantage of controlling their position and shape is proposed using a conventional lithography with a modification and pyrolysis. Field emission experiment shows the linear relation of Fowler-Nordheim (F-N) curve.

articleTitle: Simulations of terahertz coherent transition radiation by an ultrashort bunch generated from the photocathode
abstract: In this paper, the characteristics of terahertz coherent transition radiation are analyzed by the three-dimensional simulations. The results of field distributions are in agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: TWT life cycle cost reduction program
abstract: The life cycle cost of microwave tubes is a major component of the total operational cost for large radar systems. Since system requirements are almost impossible to change, cost can really only be reduced by engineering improvements to high-value components (such as microwave tubes) which result in improved life expectancy. This paper presents one such example in which modern design and analysis methods were applied to an existing TWT design. The approach was to increase the effective area of the cathode, thereby decreasing the cathode loading and extending life. Modeling and simulation codes were used throughout the process to ensure that performance would not be compromised.

articleTitle: Improvement of the field-emission characteristics of a cold cathode with nano particles
abstract: The field-emission cathode has potential application in the field emission display panels, high frequency amplifiers, X-ray sources, cathodoluminescent light sources. Many research works have been focused on the improvement of field-emission performance of a carbon nanotube cathode. A few methods, such as adhesive taping, soft rubber rolling, mechanical rubbing, plasma etching, and laser irradiating, have been proposed to get large emission current and good emission uniformity. In this paper, a new structure of the cold cathode is proposed. A metal layer is deposited on a cathode substrate as the cathode electrode. The field emitters, such as carbon nanotubes, ZnO nanopods, and etc., are grown on the cathode electrode. Some nano particles with high conductivity are distributed around the cathode electrode by spraying or printing. The result shows the distribution of electric field between a field-emission diode.

articleTitle: 0.5THz Smith-Purcell device using sheet electron beam
abstract: The two major components, sheet beam electron gun and interaction circuit, consisting the 0.5 THz Smith-Purcell device under development are being investigated in separate diagnosis systems. The thermionic cathode showed the required emission current density of 50 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and assembled into the electron gun. The interaction circuit fabricated by laser machining is being investigated using the precise electron beam from a scanning electron microscope.

articleTitle: High average power C & X - Band magnetrons
abstract: A pair of high average power magnetrons have been developed for a military application. Both C & X band devices run at 3 KW peak, 1 KW average power. The C-band device is tunable over a 200 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Study of the performance comparison between micro-chamber quadrupole mass spectrometer and miniature quadrupole mass spectrometer
abstract: In this paper, two different kinds of QMSs, micro-chamber quadrupole mass spectrometer(MCQMS) and miniature quadrupole mass spectrometer(MQMS), are compared from structure and their performance like small volume and low weight, stable working time, easy to fabricate, mass resolution and sensitivity, respectively. The analysis shows that MCQMS has better performance than that of QMS, such as smaller size, higher sensitivity and better stability. The good performance of MCQMS will make it have potential application in outer space in the near future.

articleTitle: Vacuum electronics applications at CERN
abstract: CERN operates a large number of vacuum electronics based RF power amplifiers covering a wide frequency range - over 300 sockets with 24 different grid tubes and klystrons are in use and require constant care to insure reliable operation of the accelerators. This is in particular true for the LHC and its injector chain, for which a program of improvement and stepwise upgrade has started. These include IOT's for the SPS and klystrons and modulators for Linac4 and SPL. The CLIC study and the CTF3 facility are relevant to vacuum electronics in many ways: The CLIC primary RF power, to be provided at 1 GHz, requires highest possible efficiency and phase stability, MBK's are likely candidates. The CLIC RF power source and CTF3 are themselves large vacuum electronics applications, consequently there are areas of common interest and concern, including fabrication techniques, pulse compression techniques, breakdown and multipactor theory and simulation, material fatigue, numerical analysis of slow-wave structures, vacuum compatible ceramics and damping materials, just to name a few.

articleTitle: Field emission performance of nanostructured carbon films
abstract: The field emission performance of n-type NCD films with different composition and nanostructure is investigated in detail by analyzing the different role played by composition, grain size and orientation in the attempt to identify the material better suited for cold emitters realization in terms of low voltage operation, current driving capability and stability. Different configurations of collecting electrodes are employed to verify the occurrence of nitrogen induced morphology changes and partial orientation into elongated in plane diamond domains. By increasing nitrogen content up to N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>=25% the threshold field for an electron emission current density of 1 muA/mm decreases from 25 V mum<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> down to 11 V mum<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. In addition, by comparing the field emission performance achieved for the sample with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 25% using planar and vertical electrode arrangements, a further reduction of threshold electric field from 11 to 7.5 V mum<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and much higher emission current density (up to 50 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) are found, without showing fatigue effects after prolonged emission. Thanks to the composition and to the orientation of carbon emission sites, the N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 25% UNCD film then appears the elective material for the realization of stable cold cathodes.

articleTitle: Converting low-order circular electric modes to Gaussian beams in high-frequency gyrotrons
abstract: Gyrotrons have been found to hold great promise in the enhancement of signal-to-noise ratios in Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy experiments, through the use of Dynamic Nuclear Polarization (DNP). Such applications typically require low CW output power levels (10-100 W) at frequencies ranging from 250 GHz to 1 THz. A key challenge in the design of such gyrotrons is the conversion of the excited oscillation mode into a usable Gaussian output beam. In this regime, applicable mode converter design techniques differ somewhat from those employed in the higher-power, lower-frequency fusion gyrotrons that have been a primary driver of mode converter technology in recent years. Here, several mode conversion techniques developed over the past several decades are employed to design a compact internal mode converter for generating a Gaussian beam from a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</sub> interaction mode in a 263 GHz DNP gyrotron.

articleTitle: Applications and current status of the finite-element MICHELLE gun & collector simulation code
abstract: The MICHELLE code is a finite-element electrostatic particle in cell code for application to 2D and 3D particle beam formation, transport, and collection. Its primary development focus has been for DC electron guns and depressed collectors, however, it has other applications such as RF electron guns, ion thrusters, photocathodes, etc. Its ability to manage large mesh sizes and large particle counts in complex geometries requiring the resolution of disparate spatial scales in 2D and 3D on desktop computers has allowed it to be applied to devices that could not have been readily modeled in recent years. This presentation gives an overview of recent applications, capabilities, and the current status of MICHELLE. In particular, application to time-dependent problems and optimization will be illustrated.

articleTitle: Effect of ion bombardment on the field emission of a zinc oxide cathode
abstract: The effects of ion bombardment on the field emission of screen printed tetrapod zinc oxide cathodes are reported. The field emission characteristics of this cathode degrade strongly after Ar ion bombardment for 10min at an energy of 3keV and ion current of 5µA. The emission current density decreases from 1.65 to 0.32mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 4.50V/µm field strength, while the turn-on field increases from 2.16 to 3.11V/µm at a current density of 0.1µA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This result demonstrates that the field emission of the ZnO emitters severely degrades upon ion bombardment. The emission degradation can be attributed to a lower value of the field enhancement factor β, which is caused by changes of the morphology, and a higher work function ϕ, which is caused by changes of the surface composition of ZnO.

articleTitle: Design of RF window for 42 GHz, 200kW gyrotron
abstract: This paper deals with the design of RF window for 42 GHz, 200 kW high power gyrotron. The simulation of RF window for 42 GHz gyrotron has been carried out using the Ansoft HFSS and CST microwave studio. In 42 GHz gyrotron double disc of diameter 85 mm and thickness 3.2 mm sapphire window and spacing (Coolant FC-75) of discs 2.7 mm has been used in the simulation. The return loss (S11) and insertion loss (S21) of the 42 GHz gyrotron window have been found as -47.3 dB and -0.04 dB respectively. The return loss and insertion loss of the S-band window have been found as -27.3 dB and -0.07 dB respectively at cylindrical waveguide length 33 mm. The simulated result has also been validated through experimental results for S-band window.

articleTitle: Design, fabrication, and test of an X-Band multiple beam klystron
abstract: Fabrication was completed on an X-Band multiple beam klystron (MBK) designed to produce 50 MW of RF power in microsecond pulses. The klystron incorporates a confined flow, multiple beam gun where the cathodes are located relatively far from the device axis. This required unique focusing structures to maintain beam quality. The MBK will be tested at Brookhaven National Laboratories.

articleTitle: Design of a W band transmitter for surface movement radar (SMR)
abstract: This paper describes the main features of a compact transmitter in W band. It is also highlighted the high voltage modulator designed to satisfy the strict requirements for the transmitter itself. The philosophy of the design does not cover only the hardware architecture but it also takes a look to the radar maintenance concept.

articleTitle: MAGIC FDTD-PIC code effective electromagnetic boundary for charged particle penetration
abstract: The authors address the Matched Phase Velocity method for bounding an electromagnetic domain in the MAGIC FDTD-PIC EM code. Reflected power is shown to be reduced 18 dB compared to the conventional port treatment. Boundary quality is preserved under penetration by charged particles.

articleTitle: Microstrip Meander-Line Slow Wave Structure Based on Electromagnetic Band Gap Surface
abstract: An electromagnetic band gap structures (EBGS) has been used in the Microstrip meander-line slow wave structures (MML-SWSs) in order to improve their performance. The EBGSs can be used as the substrates to support the MML-SWSs, which replace the ceramic substrates in traditional ones. The simulation results show that the minimum loss of the MML-SWSs used EBGS is half of the traditional one.

articleTitle: A design study of a permanent magnet quadrupole focused helix traveling-wave tube
abstract: Periodic permanent magnet quadrupole (PMQ) lattices have the potential to provide the strong focusing required to successfully transport higher current beams than conventional PPM lattices. We present a design example of a PMQ lattice optimized for a 16 kV, 0.81 A beam along with particle simulations using the electron transport code, MICHELLE 3D. We also present analyses of the interaction of the elliptical beam formed in the PMQ lattice with a helical traveling-wave circuit to provide insights into the advantages afforded by PMQ focusing.

articleTitle: Cyclotron protective device with increased frequency band
abstract: The authors talk about the last achievements with designing the cyclotron protective device (CPD) having a recovery time not more then 20 to 30 ns. The combination of CPD with low noise amplifier (LNA) is named as cyclotron protected complex amplifier (CPCA). It is concluded that increasing the frequency band of 3 cm wavelength CPD in twice is very important stage of development for present-day radar systems.

Author Keywords: fast cyclotron wave of electron beam

articleTitle: Enhanced field emission of tetrapod zinc oxide in methane
abstract: Tetrapod zinc oxide (T-ZnO), being a kind of nano-scale material, has a large specific surface area and high surface binding energy, which will make it sensitive to ambient gases; hence, the field emission (FE) properties of this ZnO nanomaterial will be influenced by gas adsorption. The effect of methane on the field emission of T-ZnO emitters was investigated. It was found that CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> enhanced the field emission substantially. By curve fitting we are able to describe the experimental results adequately as a function of the methane pressure. The increase of the field emission is caused by a lower work function of the ZnO-emitters.

articleTitle: Recent progress on relativistic magnetrons
abstract: We present experimental and simulation results from research on the 6-cavity, UM/L-3 relativistic magnetron, focusing on techniques to improve mode selection, power, and pulselength. Performance enhancements utilize magnetic priming, triple-point cathodes and mitigation of window flashover.

articleTitle: Microwave couplers with decreased length
abstract: The possibility to create a wave impedance transformer (coupler) with length much less the quarter wavelength is considered in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of helical slow wave structure for Ka-band 40W space TWT
abstract: A simple design approach for the slow wave structure (SWS) of a Ka-band 40 W helix TWT has been developed. Two software CST MWS and in house developed SUNRAY-1D have been used to design helical slow wave structure for meeting the desired power (>40 W), gain (>45 dB) and electronic efficiency (>14%).

articleTitle: Experimental study on hundreds of MW at X-band for relativistic backward wave oscillator (RBWO)
abstract: BWO-circuit was designed to generate hundreds MW electromagnetic wave on X-band in this study. A RF coupler is designed and fabricated to measure the power of an electromagnetic wave which is generated in the slow wave structure of a relativistic backward wave oscillator (RBWO) before this wave is radiated through an antenna. To pickup about -63 dB of total output power and avoid a RF breakdown in this coupler, a 2 mm times 5 mm slot is made in a cylindrical waveguide. This coupler is installed before the radiation antenna and the measured value is compared with the power which is measured after the radiation. In the end, the radiation pattern was identified by using of fluorescent lamps.

articleTitle: Three-stage relativistic klystron-oscillator
abstract: Simulation of a two- and three-cascade design of the oscillator on a high-current relativistic beam with electrodynamic system as a section of a hollow cylindrical waveguide with two or three sides resonant grooves are located is executed.

articleTitle: Multi beam S-band klystron with the field emitter
abstract: The design for a S-band multiple-beam klystron with field emitter is presented. The klystron will operate on 3.3 GHz, peak power 3 kW, average power 50 W. Calculation of the electron trajectories and circuit design are described.

articleTitle: Study on axially symmetric aperture lenses with extension of an inhomogeneous electric field
abstract: We analyzed a compact lens by using a modified analytical theory and three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations. In a compact lens, in which the thin lens and paraxial trajectory approximations are not acceptable, an inhomogeneous electric field can be extended to the entire region of the object and the image spaces. Computer simulations of the current density and the electron beam temperature, quantities which cannot be estimated by the analytical theory, show that an aperture lens utilizing the extended inhomogeneous electric field can possibly be used to provide a vacuum microelectronic device with a high-current-density focused electron beam of several hundred amperes per square centimeter.

articleTitle: Spurious-mode-suppressing method in cylindrical resonator for high peak power multi-beam klystron
abstract: A spurious-mode-suppressing method is introduced in this paper, aiming at increasing frequency interval between operating mode (TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">310</sub> mode) and spurious mode (TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">020</sub> mode). By means of CST-MWS, we find that the frequency interval can be increased 0.65 GHz in X-band by the method.

articleTitle: High power UHF IOT for CW and pulsed applications
abstract: A standard TV broadcast IOT from e2v technologies can easily be fitted into a tuneable circuit adapted for CW or pulsed applications enabling pulse peak powers up to 140 kW or CW powers up to 80 kW to be achieved over a frequency range of 400 MHz to 810 MHz. The IOTD2130 was first introduced for TV broadcasting in 1999 and is now used worldwide in both analogue and digital transmission applications. It provides the highest available output power of any e2v IOT and over 190 tubes are in regular service, reliably achieving >60,000 operating hours. The IOTD2130 has several features that make it ideal for CW applications. These features include direct water- cooling of the all copper internal anode, a large diameter output ceramic and a fully enclosed input circuit. This paper presents test results and performance data for CW operation of the IOTD2130 over a range of frequencies from 500 MHz to 800 MHz and pulsed performance at a frequency of 402.5 MHz.

articleTitle: Simulation research on the sheet electron beam gun
abstract: In this paper, we study the novel sheet electron beam gun by using CST simulation. We can find that the rectangular sheet electron beam gun can easily generate the rectangular sheet electron beam, its electrode shape and cathode focusing electrode angle have obvious influences on the performances of the rectangular sheet electron beam, such as its height and current density. The simulation results can offer a basis for designing a sheet electron beam gun which can be used in the high-power millimeter wave sources, such as traveling wave tubes.

articleTitle: The spectral responding characteristic research of the ultraviolet image intensifier
abstract: The ultraviolet image intensifier is a kind of vacuum image device with photocathode of Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te (Cesium Tellurium). Its spectral response characteristic curve is measured with a specially designed spectral response measuring system, the quantum efficiency is calculated, the diffusing length of the minor carriers is analyzed. At last some opinions are brought to improve the technique.

articleTitle: Defect modes in two-dimensional parallelogram lattice photonic crystals
abstract: Using plane wave method (PWM) combined with supercell method, Fourier extension coefficient of dielectric function for arbitrary defects in parallelogram lattice PC are derived, then the point and line defect modes of TM mode for 5×5 supercell PC with lattice angle 70° are calculated. These results would provide theoretical instruction for designing vacuum electron devices using PC with parallelogram lattice.
